name: Should I renovate before selling or after buying in LA?

mainEntity.name: Is it better to renovate a home before selling it or after buying it in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: Is it better to renovate a home before selling it or after buying it in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whether to renovate before selling or after buying depends on the goal. Before selling, small strategic updates often create better return than a major remodel, especially if the market already values the home’s location and layout. After buying, renovation is usually the better path when the new owner wants to customize the design, improve flow, or fix major issues that would be hard to address before closing. In Los Angeles, the decision also depends on timing and permitting. A seller usually does not want to take on long pre-construction timelines, while a buyer may prefer to plan a larger renovation after escrow closes so the design can match their needs. If the home has strong bones but outdated finishes, targeted upgrades may be enough. If the floor plan is awkward, systems are old, or structural work is needed, a post-purchase renovation is more practical. The best choice is the one that aligns with budget, timeline, and how long the owner plans to keep the property.
acceptedAnswer.description: If the goal is to maximize sale value, small targeted upgrades often make more sense before selling. If the buyer wants customization or the home needs major structural changes, renovating after purchase is usually better because it avoids trying to fit a personal plan into an existing property.
